questions.label: 1(a)
questions.stem:
Emily practices serving a volleyball directly towards the net. A high-speed camera is positioned on the side of the volleyball court. After Emily hits the ball, the camera records that the lowest point of the ball passes through the points $(1, 2.8)$, $(2, 2.86)$ and $(3, 2.89)$.
The $x$-coordinate represents the ball’s horizontal distance, in metres ($\text{m}$), from the point at which Emily hits the ball. The $y$-coordinate represents the height, $h$ metres, of the lowest point of the ball above the ground.
The height, $h$, can be modelled with an equation in the form $h(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$. Use the coordinates of the points to write down three equations in terms of $a$, $b$ and $c$.

figures.alt: Diagram (not to scale) showing a player at $x=0$ serving a volleyball. A horizontal axis is marked from $0$ to $18$ in steps of $2$, with a vertical line labelled "net" at $x=9$. Four circles show the ball at $x=0$ and at $(1, 2.8)$, $(2, 2.86)$, $(3, 2.89)$, with arrows pointing from the coordinates to the corresponding balls.

questions.stem:
The number of words that a child understands is modelled by the equation
$$y = -167 + 6264\log_{10} x, \text{ for } x \in \mathbb{R}^{+},$$
where $x$ is the number of years since the child was born, and $y$ is the number of words the child understands. Use the model to predict the number of words that a child understands when $x = 10$.

The fifth term of a geometric sequence is $48$ and the sixth term is $96$. For this sequence, find
(i) the common ratio.
(ii) the first term.

Cargo ships can only enter the Port of Savannah when the water is deep enough. The following graph shows a sinusoidal model of the depth of the water, $w$ feet, on a given day at a time $t$ hours after $00{:}00$ (midnight). The model begins at a minimum of $(0, 50.5)$ and its first maximum is at $(6.25, 57.5)$.

Write down the period of the model.

figures.alt: Graph of a sinusoidal curve $w$ (feet) against $t$ (hours) for $0 \leqslant t \leqslant 14$, labelled "diagram not to scale". The vertical axis ranges from $50$ to $58$ with a break below $50$; the horizontal axis is marked at $2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14$. The curve starts at a minimum $(0, 50.5)$, rises to a maximum at $(6.25, 57.5)$, falls to a second minimum at $(12.5, 50.5)$, and continues rising until $t = 14$.

questions.label: 5(a)
questions.stem:
TurboEats is a food delivery company that charges customers $\$0.80$ per kilometre plus a fixed amount of $\$1.50$. Their delivery charge, $T$ in $\$$, is represented by the function
$$T(x) = 0.80x + 1.50, \text{ for } x \geqslant 0,$$
where $x$ is the distance in kilometres from where the food is picked up to where it is delivered. Lorena’s home is $5.1\text{ km}$ from a pizza café. Find the charge for TurboEats to deliver a pizza from the café to her home.

questions.label: 5(b)
questions.stem:
TurboEats is a food delivery company that charges customers $\$0.80$ per kilometre plus a fixed amount of $\$1.50$. Their delivery charge, $T$ in $\$$, is represented by the function
$$T(x) = 0.80x + 1.50, \text{ for } x \geqslant 0,$$
where $x$ is the distance in kilometres from where the food is picked up to where it is delivered. A second food delivery company, GogoDart, charges customers according to the function $G(x) = ax + b$, for $x \geqslant 0$. Their charges for the first $6\text{ km}$ are shown in the following graph of $y = G(x)$. The line passes through integer grid points. (i) Write down the value of $a$.
(ii) Write down the value of $b$.

figures.alt: Line graph of $y = G(x)$ on a grid for $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 6$ and $0 \leqslant y \leqslant 8$, with integer grid lines every $1$ unit. The straight line starts at $(0, 2)$ and passes through $(1, 3)$, $(2, 4)$, $(3, 5)$, $(4, 6)$, $(5, 7)$ and $(6, 8)$.

questions.label: 6(a)
questions.stem:
Jeff is designing a garden around a corner of his house. The lengths, in metres, of each side of the garden are given in terms of $x$, as shown in the following diagram.

Show that the garden's area, $A\text{ m}^2$, is given by $A = 8x^2 + 36x$.

figures.alt: L-shaped shaded garden wrapping around the top and right sides of a white rectangular house, marked "diagram not to scale". The top horizontal edge of the garden has length $6x$, the left vertical edge above the house has length $x+4$, the right vertical edge has length $2x+10$, and the bottom horizontal edge to the right of the house has length $2x$.

Find the value of $x$.

Find the length of fence that Jeff needs.

questions.label: 7(a)
questions.stem:
Fariah wants to cover her garden with grass. She chooses Swiftlawn, which can be purchased in either rolls, which cover $1.4\text{ metres (m)}$ by $0.6\text{ m}$ when unrolled, or flats, which cover $0.6\text{ m}$ by $0.4\text{ m}$.
Fariah's garden is rectangular and measures $8\text{ m}$ by $4.8\text{ m}$, as shown in the following diagram. She wants to cover the garden with rolls and flats without extending beyond the garden's dimensions. She plans two phases for the work: phase 1 and phase 2.
In phase 1, she will lay rolls from left to right with no space between them. She will place as many complete rolls as she can, then begin a new row. She will keep adding rows until she cannot add another row. (i) Find the number of rolls Fariah will be able to lay in phase 1.
(ii) Hence, calculate the remaining area of the garden that will not be covered by the rolls.

figures.alt: Rectangle representing Fariah's garden measuring $8\text{ m}$ wide by $4.8\text{ m}$ high, with shaded rectangular rolls of dimensions $1.4\text{ m}$ by $0.6\text{ m}$ laid from left to right along the top row and starting a second row below; arrows indicate continuing across the width and down the height; not to scale.

questions.label: 7(b)
questions.stem:

Fariah's garden is rectangular and measures $8\text{ m}$ by $4.8\text{ m}$, as shown in the following diagram. She wants to cover the garden with rolls and flats without extending beyond the garden's dimensions. She plans two phases for the work: phase 1 and phase 2.
In phase 1, she will lay rolls from left to right with no space between them. She will place as many complete rolls as she can, then begin a new row. She will keep adding rows until she cannot add another row. In phase 2, Fariah will cover the remaining area of the garden using only flats. Find the number of flats Fariah will need.

figures.alt: Rectangle representing Fariah's garden measuring $8\text{ m}$ wide by $4.8\text{ m}$ high, with shaded rectangular rolls of dimensions $1.4\text{ m}$ by $0.6\text{ m}$ laid from left to right along the top row and starting a second row below; arrows indicate continuing across the width and down the height; not to scale.

questions.label: 8(a)
questions.stem:
To make a wastewater treatment plant fully functional, the flow rate of wastewater into the plant must be increased each day until the flow rate is set to a value greater than $25$ cubic metres per minute ($\text{m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$). The flow rate is set by the plant manager at the start of each day, and remains constant for the following $24$ hours.
On day $1$, the flow rate is set to $2.5\text{ m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$. The following table shows the flow rate for each of the first three days.
Day: $1, 2, 3$; Flow rate ($\text{m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$): $2.5, 3.5, 4.9$, paired in that order. Show that these flow rates form a geometric sequence.

questions.label: 8(b)
questions.stem:
To make a wastewater treatment plant fully functional, the flow rate of wastewater into the plant must be increased each day until the flow rate is set to a value greater than $25$ cubic metres per minute ($\text{m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$). The flow rate is set by the plant manager at the start of each day, and remains constant for the following $24$ hours.
On day $1$, the flow rate is set to $2.5\text{ m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$. The following table shows the flow rate for each of the first three days.
Day: $1, 2, 3$; Flow rate ($\text{m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$): $2.5, 3.5, 4.9$, paired in that order. This geometric sequence continues until day $n$, when the flow rate is first set to a value greater than $25\text{ m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$. Find the value of $n$.

questions.label: 8(c)
questions.stem:
To make a wastewater treatment plant fully functional, the flow rate of wastewater into the plant must be increased each day until the flow rate is set to a value greater than $25$ cubic metres per minute ($\text{m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$). The flow rate is set by the plant manager at the start of each day, and remains constant for the following $24$ hours.
On day $1$, the flow rate is set to $2.5\text{ m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$. The following table shows the flow rate for each of the first three days.
Day: $1, 2, 3$; Flow rate ($\text{m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$): $2.5, 3.5, 4.9$, paired in that order. The plant manager is required to report the total volume of wastewater that flows into the plant from the start of day $1$ until the end of day $n$. (i) Find the sum of the flow rates for the first $n$ days, in $\text{m}^3\text{ min}^{-1}$.
(ii) Hence, or otherwise, find the total volume of wastewater in $\text{m}^3$ that flows into the plant during this time.

questions.label: 9(a)
questions.stem:
A group of friends want to rent a beach house for their vacation. The cost per person, $c$, varies inversely with the total number of people, $n$, who will be sharing the cost.
If four people share the cost equally, then the cost per person is $\$187.50$. Determine an equation for $c$ in terms of $n$.

questions.label: 9(b)
questions.stem:
A group of friends want to rent a beach house for their vacation. The cost per person, $c$, varies inversely with the total number of people, $n$, who will be sharing the cost.
If four people share the cost equally, then the cost per person is $\$187.50$. The group wants the cost per person to be less than $\$100.00$. (i) Find the minimum number of people needed to share the cost to meet this requirement.
(ii) Find the cost per person for this number of people.

questions.label: 10(a)
questions.stem:
Mikko deposits $\$10\,000$ into a savings account with a fixed nominal annual interest rate of $r\%$ compounded monthly. At the end of each month, he deposits $\$800$ into the account.
After $10$ years, the value in the savings account is $\$160\,000$. Find the value of $r$.

questions.label: 10(b)
questions.stem:
Mikko deposits $\$10\,000$ into a savings account with a fixed nominal annual interest rate of $r\%$ compounded monthly. At the end of each month, he deposits $\$800$ into the account.
After $10$ years, the value in the savings account is $\$160\,000$. Find the amount of interest earned over the $10$ years.

questions.label: 11(a)
questions.stem:
The first term of an arithmetic sequence is $18$ and its common difference is $7$.

Find the $42^{\text{nd}}$ term of the sequence.

questions.label: 11(b)
questions.stem:
The first term of an arithmetic sequence is $18$ and its common difference is $7$. The sum of the first $n$ terms of the sequence is $9475$. Find a quadratic equation in terms of $n$ that represents this information.
Give your answer in the form $an^2 + bn + c = 0$.

questions.label: 12(a)
questions.stem:
A function is defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{4}{x} - 3$, for $-6 \leqslant x \leqslant 10, x \neq 0$.

Find $f(10)$.

questions.label: 12(b)
questions.stem:
A function is defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{4}{x} - 3$, for $-6 \leqslant x \leqslant 10, x \neq 0$.

Find the range of $f$.

questions.label: 12(c)
questions.stem:
A function is defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{4}{x} - 3$, for $-6 \leqslant x \leqslant 10, x \neq 0$.

Find $f^{-1}(-2)$.

Give your answers to parts (a), (b) and (d) correct to two decimal places.
Suriyana invests $\text{GBP } 14\,500$ into an account that pays a nominal annual interest rate of $2.3\%$, compounded monthly. Calculate the amount Suriyana will have in her account after three years.

questions.label: 14(a)
questions.stem:
Sheena purchased a new mobile phone. The value of Sheena's mobile phone, $V$ in Philippine Pesos ($\text{PHP}$), can be modelled by the function
$$V(t) = 2000 + 30\,000\left(\mathrm{e}^{-kt}\right)\text{, for } t \geqslant 0,$$
where $t$ is the time, in months, after the mobile phone was purchased. Calculate the value of the mobile phone when it was purchased.

questions.label: 14(b)
questions.stem:
Sheena purchased a new mobile phone. The value of Sheena's mobile phone, $V$ in Philippine Pesos ($\text{PHP}$), can be modelled by the function
$$V(t) = 2000 + 30\,000\left(\mathrm{e}^{-kt}\right)\text{, for } t \geqslant 0,$$
where $t$ is the time, in months, after the mobile phone was purchased. Ten months after it was purchased, the value of the mobile phone has decreased by $40\%$. Find the value of $k$.

Eduardo takes a photograph of a water fountain. He notices the path of the water looks like a parabola, and he decides to model the curve using the equation

$$y = ax^2 + bx + c.$$

Eduardo takes measurements from the photograph. He finds the distance between the $x$-intercepts, $\mathrm{R}$ and $\mathrm{S}$, to be $3\text{ cm}$ and the maximum height of the water to be $13\text{ cm}$ above the fountain.

These measurements are shown on the following diagram, where the point $(0, 0)$ is indicated as $\mathrm{O}$ and the vertex, $\mathrm{T}$, is on the $y$-axis. Write down the value of $c$.

figures.alt: Diagram (not to scale) of the parabolic path of water from a fountain on $(x,y)$ axes. The $x$-axis passes through points $\mathrm{R}$, $\mathrm{O}(0,0)$, and $\mathrm{S}$ with the distance between $\mathrm{R}$ and $\mathrm{S}$ labelled $3\text{ cm}$. The vertex $\mathrm{T}$ lies on the positive $y$-axis, and the vertical height from the $x$-axis to $\mathrm{T}$ is labelled $13\text{ cm}$. A water fountain is drawn beneath $\mathrm{S}$ and a splash beneath $\mathrm{R}$.
